Umayyad Caliphate.fact: In 734, al-Harith ibn Surayj led a revolt that received broad backing from Arab settlers and native inhabitants alike, capturing Balkh but failing to take Merv. After this defeat, al-Harith's movement seems to have been dissolved.

Umayyad Caliphate.question: In 744, Yazid III, a son of al-Walid I, was proclaimed caliph in _____, while his army killed al-Walid II
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: In 744, Yazid III, a son of al-Walid I, was proclaimed caliph in Damascus, while his army killed al-Walid II. Umayyad Caliphate.question: A rebellion soon broke out in Syria, perhaps due to resentment over the relocation of the capital, and in 746 Marwan razed the walls of Homs and _____ in retaliation
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Yazid had appointed his brother, Ibrahim, as his successor, but Marwan II (744–750), the grandson of Marwan I, led an army from the northern frontier and entered Damascus in December 744, where he was proclaimed caliph. Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Yusufzai.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Yusufzai.question: The Mughal Khel have ruled and held the position of maliks in _____ for more than 300 years
Yusufzai.fact: The Mughal Khel have ruled and held the position of maliks in Ghoriwala for more than 300 years. As the author of Bannu Gazetteer said: The most notable case of the sort is that of the Mughal Khels of Ghoriwala, a Yousafzai group, who conquered territory for themselves seven generations ago and still preserve in speech and physiognomy proof of their origin.

Yusufzai.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Yusufzai.question: In the 19th century, the distinction between hamsāya as a "dependent _____ tribe" and faqīr as "non-Pashtun landless peasants" became blurred
Yusufzai.fact: Hamsāya The hamsāya or "shade sharers" were the clients or dependents from other (non-Yusufzai) Pashtun tribes who became attached to the Yusufzai tribe over the years. Faqīr The faqīr or "poor" were the non-Pashtun landless peasants who were assigned to the Yusufzai landowners.

Yusufzai.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Yusufzai.question: In 1757, he supported _____ in his attack on Delhi
Yusufzai.fact: In 1757, he supported Ahmad Shah Durrani in his attack on Delhi. After his victory, Ahmad Shah Durrani re-installed the Mughal emperor Alamgir II on the Delhi throne as the titular Mughal head, but gave the actual control of Delhi to Najib ad-Daula.

Yusufzai.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Yusufzai.question: In 1761, he took part in the _____ of Panipat and provided thousands of Rohilla troops and many guns to Ahmad Shah Durrani to defeat the Marathas
Yusufzai.fact: In 1761, he took part in the Third Battle of Panipat and provided thousands of Rohilla troops and many guns to Ahmad Shah Durrani to defeat the Marathas.

Yusufzai.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Yusufzai.question: After his death in 1770, Najib ad-Dawlah was succeeded by his son, _____, who was defeated in 1772 by a joint Mughal-Maratha force, forcing him to flee from Rohilkhand
Yusufzai.fact: After his death in 1770, Najib ad-Dawlah was succeeded by his son, Zabita Khan, who was defeated in 1772 by a joint Mughal-Maratha force, forcing him to flee from Rohilkhand.

Yusufzai.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Yusufzai.question: In 1897, the _____ annexed Dir and granted the title of the "Nawab of Dir" to Sharif Khan Akhundkhel, the ruler of Dir (1886–1904)
Yusufzai.fact: In 1897, the British Raj annexed Dir and granted the title of the "Nawab of Dir" to Sharif Khan Akhundkhel, the ruler of Dir (1886–1904).

Yusufzai.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Yusufzai.question: The princely state of Dir existed until 1969, after which they were merged into _____, and then in 1970 into the North-West Frontier Province (present-day Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) of Pakistan
Yusufzai.fact: The princely state of Dir existed until 1969, after which they were merged into West Pakistan, and then in 1970 into the North-West Frontier Province (present-day Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) of Pakistan.

Yusufzai.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Yusufzai.question: In 1586, Akbar the Great tried to invade _____ in the Battle of the Malandari Pass (1586) but failed and it become the greatest disaster to Mughal empire in the era of Akbar
Yusufzai.fact: In 1586, Akbar the Great tried to invade Malakand in the Battle of the Malandari Pass (1586) but failed and it become the greatest disaster to Mughal empire in the era of Akbar.

Yusufzai.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Yusufzai.question: From 1757 to 1770, Najib ad-Daula served as the governor of _____, also ruling over Dehradun
Yusufzai.fact: From 1757 to 1770, Najib ad-Daula served as the governor of Saharanpur, also ruling over Dehradun.

Yusufzai.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Yusufzai.question: Through a regular rotation of ownership, the Yusufzai landowners would migrate for up to _____ for their new share after each cycle, although the tenants cultivating the land would stay on
Yusufzai.fact: Through a regular rotation of ownership, the Yusufzai landowners would migrate for up to 30 miles for their new share after each cycle, although the tenants cultivating the land would stay on.

École Spéciale d'Architecture.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
École Spéciale d'Architecture.question: It was endorsed by Eugène _____-le-Duc, a childhood friend, who after many infructuous attempts at reforming the École des Beaux-Arts had imagined the idea in 1863
École Spéciale d'Architecture.fact: It was endorsed by Eugène Viollet-le-Duc, a childhood friend, who after many infructuous attempts at reforming the École des Beaux-Arts had imagined the idea in 1863. Viollet le Duc provided many of the educational precepts and became one of its original stockholders, along with other notables including : Ferdinand de Lesseps, Anatole de Baudot, Eugène Flachat, Dupont de l'Eure, Jean-Baptiste André Godin, and Émile Muller.
